A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SURE framework and mitigation study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are readable and support a reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original robustness evaluations, scaling experiments, SFT/DPO mitigation results, and the feature-distribution experiments and K-S tests in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds an attention analysis comparing Robust, Win, and Lose examples in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The SURE perturbation pipeline, bidirectional entailment and answer-preservation filters, and SFT/DPO training objectives and sample construction remain unchanged. The added attention measurement is a diagnostic analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ-open/Wikipedia for SURE_Wiki and SIG_Wiki, and TriviaQA/Bing web documents for SIG_Trivial, with the same QA tasks and perturbation coverage. The new attention analysis reuses SIG_Wiki.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same model families, Chain-of-Note, DeepSeek-R1/V3, and SFT/DPO variants. The Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct judge identified in v3's main text was already specified in v2 Appendix G.

E3.justification: The reported training protocol for both mitigation methods is substantially revised. v2 Table 10 specifies learning rate 2e-5, effective batch size 32, sequence length 4096, and 100 warmup steps; v3 Table 11 specifies SFT/DPO rates 1e-5/5e-6, batches 64/16, length 8192, and warmup ratio 0.1. These revisions do not establish reruns. v3 also adds an attention protocol sampling 50 golden-document examples per Robust/Win/Lose group.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a targeted analysis testing whether attention shifts toward ground-truth answer spans differ between stable and changed predictions. Existing scaling, retrieval-setting, judge-agreement, and preliminary feature-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds a Welch's t-test comparing attention differences in Robust versus combined Win/Lose examples, reporting p=0.046. Appendix K-S table captions newly explain the significance stars. Existing K-S procedures remain unchanged, and neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, mitigation, scaling, and K-S results are unchanged after matching displays. New Table 4 reports mean attention differences of 6.52e-5, 9.94e-5, and 1.15e-4 for Robust, Win, and Lose groups. Section 4.3 also newly reports GPT-4o's 89% robustness on datasource(twitter).

T1.justification: v3 introduces Equation (4), defining the attention-difference measure ΔA = |Aorg − Apert| for the new analysis. Existing mathematical formulations and robustness definitions are retained; Appendix A's oracle-score equation is merely renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about comprehensive SURE evaluation, lightweight benchmarking, effective training-based mitigation, and widespread sensitivity to spurious features.

C2.justification: v3 links attention shifts and reduced answer-span attention in Lose cases to an explanation of prediction instability. It also explicitly discusses metadata robustness receiving little benefit from scaling. The stated taxonomy limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly discloses selection of 500 Mistral-known and 500 Mistral-unknown NQ queries. Appendix H adds DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 and separate SFT/DPO specifications. These clarify and revise existing implementation documentation; the code-access link is unchanged. Appendix G's new judge-prompt figure reference is unresolved.

R1.justification: v3 adds references covering DPO, attention and interpretability, readability, and LLM judging, including Rafailov et al. (2023), Liu et al. (2025), and Zhang et al. (2026). Section 2 and the central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses Appendix A.3's repeated methodological and K-S explanations, swaps the experimental-setup and dataset-statistics appendices D/E, and updates affiliations and correspondence details. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds attention Table 4, restructures the training table into separate SFT/DPO columns, and expands K-S captions with significance legends. Several retained displays move with the text; existing figures and plotted content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful statistical evidence connecting attention shifts with response changes and clarifies query selection and per-method training specifications. These modest gains improve explanatory support and documentation. Their value is limited by unspecified model/head/layer choices in the attention analysis, training-setting revisions left unreconciled with unchanged scores, and Appendix G's unresolved prompt-figure reference.
